tribe: Banu Sa'd ibn Zayd Manat of Tamim — client of Banu Zuhra
era: The Blacksmith Who Would Not Recant
teaser: He asked the Prophet ﷺ for help and was told to wait. Forty years later he had forty thousand and wept.
quran_mention: The ayah about al-As ibn Wa'il, who withheld a debt over faith — Quran 19:77-80

layers.title: Who He Was
layers.subtitle: Taken as a boy, sold in Makka, taught a trade
layers.content:
His lineage runs back into Tamim: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt ibn Jandala ibn Sa'd ibn Khuzayma ibn Ka'b, from Banu Sa'd ibn Zayd Manat. Al-Waqidi received that chain from Khabbab's own descendants, and noted that Khabbab's child gave the same.

None of it helped him. He was captured as a boy and sold in Makka. Umm Anmar of Khuza'a bought him. Through her household he was counted an ally of Banu Zuhra, which is a technical description of a man attached to a clan without being of it. Her son Siba' ibn Abd al-Uzza was later killed by Hamza at Uhud, fighting against the Muslims — that was the family Khabbab belonged to on paper.

His kunya was Abu Abdullah. His trade was iron. He said it himself, in a report that came down through al-A'mash: 'I was a smith.' He forged swords in a city that would soon use them on him.

That is the shape of his early life. Noble ancestry he could not invoke, a foreign city, an owner, and a skill in his hands. The hands were the only part of it that was his.
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Conversion
layers.subtitle: He came in before there was a house to come into
layers.content:
Yazid ibn Ruman fixes his date with unusual precision: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt became Muslim before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the house of al-Arqam, and before he called people in it. There was no gathering yet. He believed while Islam was still being carried from one person to another by hand.

Mujahid's list of the seven who first displayed Islam openly names him fourth, after the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr and Bilal. Urwa ibn az-Zubayr's report says plainly what followed: Khabbab was one of those victimised who were tortured in Makka to force him to recant.

The cost showed up first as money. He had done work for al-As ibn Wa'il and was owed for it. He went to collect. Al-As told him: I will not settle it until you reject Muhammad. Khabbab answered, I will not reject him even if you die and are resurrected. Al-As, mocking, said that if he were resurrected he would settle it then, when he had returned to his wealth and children.

And an ayah came down about that exchange.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 19:77 — «أَفَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ بِآيَاتِنَا وَقَالَ لَأُوتَيَنَّ مَالًا وَوَلَدًا» — 'Have you seen the one who rejected Our signs and said, "I will certainly be given wealth and children"?' The passage runs to ayah 80: 'and he will come to Us alone'
layers.hadith_ref: Reported from Masruq through Abu ad-Duha and al-A'mash — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III (Yazid ibn Ruman, Urwa ibn az-Zubayr, al-A'mash)

layers.title: With the Prophet ﷺ
layers.subtitle: The man teaching Ta-Ha when Umar kicked the door in
layers.content:
Khabbab could not read a room, but he could read the Qur'an, and in Makka that made him a teacher. He was sitting with Fatima bint al-Khattab and her husband, taking them through Surah Ta-Ha from loose pages, when they heard Umar coming.

Khabbab hid inside the house. What followed he heard rather than saw: Umar's accusation, the blow, the sister's face bleeding, her declaration of faith, Umar demanding the pages, being told only the pure may touch them, going to wash. Then Umar reading until he reached 'I am Allah. There is no god but Me, so worship Me and establish the prayer to remember Me' — and saying, take me to Muhammad.

At that Khabbab came out of concealment. He is the one who told Umar what he had walked into: I hope you will be the answer to the supplication of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, for he said, O Allah, strengthen Islam by Umar ibn al-Khattab or Amr ibn Hisham. Reports differ on which night the dua was made.

He emigrated to Madinah and lodged with Kulthum ibn al-Hidm, then with Sa'd ibn Ubada. He was at Badr, Uhud, the Ditch, and every expedition after.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 20:14 — «إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدْنِي وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ لِذِكْرِي» — 'Indeed I am Allah. There is no god but Me, so worship Me and establish the prayer for My remembrance'
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III; al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Open Preaching)

layers.title: The Trial
layers.subtitle: He asked for help and was told the answer was slow
layers.content:
Al-Mubarakpuri lists the methods used on him: seized by the hair and dragged, twisted by the neck, thrown into fire, then dragged through the fire, and they did not stop until his back was burnt.

Khabbab's own account, through ash-Sha'bi, is quieter. Years later Umar seated him on his own cushion and said there was no one on earth more entitled to that assembly except one man — Bilal. Khabbab did not accept the ranking. 'Amir al-Mu'minin, there is no one more entitled than me. Bilal had those among the idolaters whom Allah protected him by. I had no one to protect me. I remember one day when they took me and kindled a fire and burned me with it, and a man put his foot on my chest.' Then he uncovered his back, and it was white like leprosy. In another version of the same meeting Umar names Ammar ibn Yasir instead.

Somewhere in those years he went to the Prophet ﷺ, who was resting on his cloak in the shade of the Ka'bah, and asked: why do you not call upon Allah? The Prophet ﷺ sat up. His face reddened. He spoke about men before them combed with iron combs down to the bone who did not change their religion, and about a day when a rider would travel from San'a to Hadramawt fearing nothing but Allah. Then: 'yet you are a hasty people.'

He had asked for relief and was given a timetable he would not live inside.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 2:214 — «حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَ الرَّسُولُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ مَتَىٰ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ ۗ أَلَا إِنَّ نَصْرَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ» — 'until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?" Truly, the help of Allah is near'
layers.hadith_ref: Sahih al-Bukhari — narrated by Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, cited by al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
layers.source: al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (citing Sahih al-Bukhari); Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III (ash-Sha'bi, Abu Layla al-Kindi)

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: Forty thousand in a chest, and a man weeping over it
layers.content:
The rider did eventually travel safely from San'a to Hadramawt. Khabbab saw it, and it frightened him.

Haritha ibn Mudarrib found him ill, cauterised seven times on the belly, saying: had I not heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbid wishing for death, I would have wished for it. They brought him a shroud of fine Egyptian linen and he wept — because Hamza had been shrouded in one cloak, and when it covered his head his feet showed. Then he said the thing that should be read slowly: 'I remember when I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and I did not own a dinar or a dirham. In the corner of my house, in my chest, are forty thousand uqiyyas. I fear that our good things have been hastened for us in the life of this world.'

Companions came to comfort him: good news, Abu Abdullah, tomorrow you go to your brothers. He wept again. Those men passed with their wages intact. He feared his had been paid early.

He died in 37 AH aged seventy-three. It is reported that Ali prayed over him on his return from Siffin, the first man he buried in Kufa. Khabbab had asked his son to bury him out at Zuhr, so that people would say a Companion was buried there and would follow — and they did. Years later the Khawarij waylaid the road and killed that son, Abdullah ibn Khabbab, and Ali moved against them at an-Nahrawan.

May Allah be pleased with him. He was afraid of comfort in a way we no longer know how to be.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 46:20 — «أَذْهَبْتُمْ طَيِّبَاتِكُمْ فِي حَيَاتِكُمُ الدُّنْيَا» — 'You consumed your good things in your worldly life.' His words echo this ayah; the sources do not say it was revealed about him
layers.hadith_ref: 'It is not proper for anyone to wish for death' — narrated by Khabbab ibn al-Aratt from the Prophet ﷺ, in Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III (Haritha ibn Mudarrib; Qays ibn Abi Hazim)
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

options.text: He was a smith, working iron
He was a tanner
He was a caravan guide
He was a scribe

quiz.citation: Khabbab's own words, reported from Masruq through Abu ad-Duha and al-A'mash, in Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He said simply, 'I was a smith.' The debt that al-As ibn Wa'il refused to pay him was almost certainly for metalwork. His skill was also what made him useful enough to keep alive.

quiz.prompt: What did al-As ibn Wa'il demand before he would settle Khabbab's debt?

options.text: That Khabbab leave Makka
That Khabbab reject Muhammad ﷺ
That Khabbab forge weapons for Quraysh
That Khabbab bring a Qurayshi guarantor

quiz.citation: Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III; the exchange is connected to Quran 19:77-80
quiz.scholar_reflection: Khabbab's reply was: I will not reject him even if you die and are resurrected. Al-As turned that into a joke about his wealth in the next life, and the joke ended up in the Qur'an.

quiz.prompt: What was Khabbab doing in Fatima bint al-Khattab's house when Umar arrived?

options.text: Repairing a sword
Hiding from Abu Jahl
Teaching them Surah Ta-Ha from written pages
Delivering a message from the Prophet ﷺ

quiz.citation: Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III; al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
quiz.scholar_reflection: He hid when he heard Umar, and came out only when he heard Umar ask to be taken to the Prophet ﷺ. Then he was the one who told Umar about the supplication that had named him.

quiz.prompt: When Umar seated him on his cushion and said only one man had more right to that place, how did Khabbab respond?

options.text: He accepted the ranking in silence
He disagreed, and uncovered his back to show why
He left the assembly
He asked for a share of the treasury instead

quiz.citation: Reported from ash-Sha'bi through Mujalid, in Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: His argument was specific: Bilal had people among the idolaters through whom Allah protected him, and Khabbab had no one. His back was white like leprosy from being burnt. Another version of the meeting names Ammar instead of Bilal.

quiz.prompt: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when Khabbab, in the shade of the Ka'bah, asked why he did not call upon Allah for help?

options.text: That help would come within the year
That the Muslims should leave Makka at once
That earlier believers were combed with iron combs and did not change, and 'you are a hasty people'
That he had already made the dua and it had been refused

quiz.citation: Sahih al-Bukhari, narrated by Khabbab ibn al-Aratt — cited in al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
quiz.scholar_reflection: He sat up and his face reddened. The promise he gave was real — a rider going safely from San'a to Hadramawt — but it was decades away, and he did not pretend otherwise.

quiz.prompt: Khabbab asked for relief and was told, in effect, not yet. How do you take that answer?

options.text: Badly. I keep asking and start doubting.
I accept it but I do not understand it
The delay has taught me more than a quick answer would
I have stopped asking for timing and only ask for strength

quiz.citation: Reflection on Sahih al-Bukhari, narrated by Khabbab ibn al-Aratt
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Prophet ﷺ did not soften it. He named the cost, named the outcome, and named the flaw in the question. Being told you are hasty is not the same as being told you are wrong to ask.

quiz.prompt: He wept at a good shroud because he remembered Hamza had a poor one. What comfort in your life would you struggle to enjoy if you thought about who never had it?

options.text: Food. I know what most of the world eats.
Safety. Mine was inherited, not earned.
Honestly, I enjoy all of it and rarely think this way
The ease of practising my deen openly

quiz.citation: Reported from Haritha ibn Mudarrib, in Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He was not performing humility. He was doing arithmetic, and he did not like the total. Forty thousand uqiyyas in a chest, against a memory of owning no dinar and no dirham.

quiz.prompt: Khabbab refused to let Umar rank Bilal above him, and gave his reasons out loud. Is that pride, or accuracy?

options.text: Accuracy. He had earned the right to correct the record.
Pride, and the sources record it without hiding it
Both at once, which is what makes it human
I would never have said it, and I am not sure that is better

quiz.citation: Reported from ash-Sha'bi, in Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He did not diminish Bilal. He pointed out a structural difference: Bilal had someone, and he had no one. That is a fact about protection, not a claim about faith.

quiz.prompt: He was told 'tomorrow you go to your brothers' and it made him weep rather than smile. When someone reassures you, what does it usually stir?

options.text: Relief. I need to hear it.
Suspicion that they do not know the full picture
A sharper awareness of the gap between me and the comparison
Nothing much. I let it pass.

quiz.citation: Reported from Tariq ibn Shihab through Qays ibn Muslim, in Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He explained the tears carefully so they would not misread them: not alarm at dying, but the word 'brothers'. He was not sure he belonged in the sentence.

quiz.prompt: He asked to be buried out at Zuhr so that others would follow him there. What are you doing now that is meant mainly to make something easier for the people after you?

options.text: Something in my family — a habit I am trying to normalise
Work that will outlast my name being attached to it
Nothing yet, and this question has landed
Being the first in my circle to do a thing openly

quiz.citation: Reported from Ibn al-Khabbab, in Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: His reasoning was tactical: bury me there and people will say a Companion is buried at Zuhr, and then they will bury their dead there too. He used his own funeral as a precedent, and it worked.
